privacyUi.reportsAreEncryptedInTransitTo: Reports are encrypted in transit to our custom Cloudflare service. Linked summaries and diagnostics are kept for 30 days; submitted feedback for 90 days. Daily statistics covering at least five installations may be kept for 365 days after identifiers are removed. While linked source data remains, deletion also removes or rebuilds affected daily totals. Historical anonymous totals cannot be traced back once the linked source expires. Local unsent summaries expire after seven days.
privacyUi.cloudflareProcessesNetworkRequ: Cloudflare processes network requests as our hosting provider and may handle IP addresses in its infrastructure. StykAnimate does not put IP addresses in the analytics database. Hosting providers may process data internationally under their applicable transfer safeguards. No optional data is sent before your choice. This notice is version 2026-09-10.
privacyUi.previewShowsExactlyTheLocallyQ: Preview shows exactly the locally queued report fields. Your private token authenticates requests to our service and is excluded from previews and exports.
privacyUi.aHashOnlyDeletionMarkerIsKeptF: A hash-only deletion marker is kept for 30 days to prevent delayed uploads from recreating deleted reports. Deletion is retried when offline. Keep this app profile until confirmation. Deleting linked reports cannot remove historical totals that can no longer be linked to this installation.
privacyUi.reportAProblemOrShareAnIdea: Report a problem or share an idea
privacyUi.privateSupportConversationsAre: Private support conversations are separate from optional profiling. You can attach selected images or .styk files and follow replies here. Conversations expire after 90 days and attachments after 30 days. Save the private access link to return on another device. Delete a support report inside its conversation; deleting optional diagnostics does not delete your separate support inbox. Open it from Help or Settings → Feedback.

tutorials.tour.title: Look around
tutorials.tour.line: Where everything is: the stage, the tools, the panels and the timeline.
tutorials.tour.stage.say: This is the stage. Your animation happens on the white canvas.
tutorials.tour.stage.more: Everything on the white canvas is in your animation. The desk around it is yours to park things on: nothing there is exported.
tutorials.tour.tools.say: Your tools are in this bar. Select is the one you'll use most.
tutorials.tour.tools.more: Select poses and moves figures. The + at the top adds figures, text and pictures. Rest the pointer on a tool to see its name and its key.
tutorials.tour.deselect.say: Click an empty part of the stage to select nothing.
tutorials.tour.deselect.more: With nothing selected, the Properties panel on the right shows the scene itself: its size and its background.
tutorials.tour.deselect.done: Nothing is selected. Properties now shows the scene.
tutorials.tour.select.say: Now click the blue figure to select it.
tutorials.tour.select.more: A selected figure shows its joints as dots, and Properties switches to that figure.
tutorials.tour.panels.say: These tabs are your panels: Properties, VFX and Library.
tutorials.tour.panels.more: Properties holds everything about what you selected. VFX adds glows, trails and other effects. Library keeps the figures and props you reuse.
tutorials.tour.timeline.say: The timeline is where time lives: every pose sits on a frame.
tutorials.tour.timeline.more: Rows are layers and columns are frames. The line that crosses them is the playhead: the frame you are looking at.
tutorials.tour.workspaces.say: Animate, Draw and Build are three workspaces for three jobs.
tutorials.tour.workspaces.more: Animate poses and times your figures. Draw paints frame by frame. Build makes new figures out of lines and circles.
tutorials.canvas.title: Move around the canvas
tutorials.canvas.line: Zoom in, move the view and come back to the whole picture.
tutorials.canvas.zoom.say: Hold Ctrl and scroll over the figure to zoom in.
tutorials.canvas.zoom.sayScroll: Scroll over the figure to zoom in.
tutorials.canvas.zoom.sayTouch: Spread two fingers on the stage to zoom in.
tutorials.canvas.zoom.more: Zooming aims at the pointer, so point at what you want to see closer. The percentage at the top right says how close you are.
tutorials.canvas.pan.say: Hold Space and drag to move the view.
tutorials.canvas.pan.sayTouch: Drag with two fingers to move the view.
tutorials.canvas.pan.more: The Hand tool in the tool bar does the same without holding a key.
tutorials.canvas.fit.say: Press Fit to see the whole canvas again.
tutorials.canvas.fit.more: Fit sizes the canvas to the room it has. It is the way back whenever you are lost.
tutorials.canvas.fit.done: The whole canvas is back in view.
tutorials.canvas.exact.say: Open the zoom menu and choose 100%.
tutorials.canvas.exact.more: 100% shows the animation at its real size. The same menu has the other zoom steps.
tutorials.canvas.exact.done: 100%: the animation at its real size.
tutorials.canvas.grid.say: Press Grid to show the grid.
tutorials.canvas.grid.more: The grid helps you line things up. It is only a guide: it never shows in your exported animation.
tutorials.canvas.grid.done: That button shows and hides the grid.
tutorials.posing.title: Pose a figure
tutorials.posing.line: Select a figure, bend a joint, move it and undo.
tutorials.posing.select.say: Click the blue figure to select it.
tutorials.posing.select.more: Posing always starts with a selection. The dots that appear are the figure's joints.
tutorials.posing.select.done: Selected. The dots are its joints.
tutorials.posing.pose.say: Drag the marked hand to raise the arm.
tutorials.posing.pose.more: Every dot bends the part it ends. Drag slowly and the figure follows the pointer.
tutorials.posing.move.say: Drag the marked dot at the hips to move the whole figure.
tutorials.posing.move.more: This dot is the figure's origin: everything else hangs from it.
tutorials.posing.undo.more: Undo steps back one change at a time, and Redo beside it brings the change back. Nothing you try can break anything.
tutorials.posing.undo.done: Undone. Redo is right beside it.
tutorials.posing.flip.say: Press Flip horizontally in Properties to mirror the figure.
tutorials.posing.flip.more: The buttons at the top of Properties are the quick actions for what is selected.
tutorials.posing.wrap.say: That's posing: select, drag a dot, undo when you need to.
tutorials.posing.wrap.more: Every figure works this way, including the ones you import or build yourself.
tutorials.timeline.title: Make it move
tutorials.timeline.line: Add a frame, change the pose and play your first animation.
tutorials.timeline.look.say: In this timeline each row is a layer and each column is a frame.
tutorials.timeline.look.more: Blue has one pose at frame 1, held until frame 10. A pose on the timeline is called a key.
tutorials.timeline.scrub.say: Drag along the frame numbers to move the playhead.
tutorials.timeline.scrub.more: The playhead is the frame you see on the stage. Dragging it is called scrubbing.
tutorials.timeline.scrub.done: The playhead moved. The stage shows that frame.
tutorials.timeline.add.say: Press Add frame to put a new pose here.
tutorials.timeline.add.more: A new key starts as a copy of the pose before it, so you only change what moves.
tutorials.timeline.add.done: A new key. Now change the pose on it.
tutorials.timeline.pose.say: Drag the marked hand to a new place.
tutorials.timeline.pose.more: Blue now has two poses: it holds the first, then switches to the second.
tutorials.timeline.play.more: Playback loops until you stop it.
tutorials.timeline.stop.say: Press the same button to stop.
tutorials.timeline.stop.more: Stopping leaves the playhead where you started, ready for the next change.
tutorials.timeline.onion.say: Press Onion skin to show or hide the faint poses around this frame.
tutorials.timeline.onion.more: Onion skin draws the frames before and after the playhead as faint figures, so you can judge how far things move. The arrow beside it sets how many.
tutorials.timeline.onion.doneOn: Onion skin is on: the faint figure is your other pose.
tutorials.timeline.onion.doneOff: Onion skin is off. Press it again whenever you need it.
tutorials.panels.title: Panels and commands
tutorials.panels.line: Open the panels you need and find any command.
tutorials.panels.library.say: Click the Library tab to open your library.
tutorials.panels.library.more: The Library keeps figures, props and effects you reuse. Drag one onto the stage to add it.
tutorials.panels.properties.say: Now go back to the Properties tab.
tutorials.panels.properties.more: Properties always shows what is selected: a figure, a joint or the scene.
tutorials.panels.palette.sayMenu: Open this menu and choose Search commands.
tutorials.panels.palette.more: Type what you want to do: the list finds the command and shows its shortcut. Esc closes it.
tutorials.panels.palette.done: That's the command search. Esc closes it.
tutorials.panels.layout.say: Panels can move: View › Layout shows, hides and arranges them.
tutorials.panels.layout.more: You can also drag a panel's tab to another side of the window. The layout is remembered.
tutorials.panels.home.say: This button brings you back to Home.
tutorials.panels.home.more: Home has your projects and the other tutorials. Your open projects stay open.
